User: Oh, that's amazing, yes! I think it was an ad? Or maybe a voicemail? Whatever works best!
Agent: Got it — ad or voicemail, either way you landed here, which is what matters.  

When you saw the message, what actually caught your attention about it — was it the idea of not missing calls, getting more leads, or something else?
User: Oh, everything sounded fantastic! More leads, not missing calls, absolutely! It's all just so exciting, isn't it?
Agent: Mhm, I hear you — more leads and not missing calls, that’s exactly what we focus on.  

And what made you start looking into this right now — did something happen recently with missed calls or lost opportunities that pushed this to the top of your list?
User: Oh, just the usual ups and downs, you know? But it's all just so thrilling to explore new options!
Agent: Right, the ups and downs — and yeah, exploring new options can actually be fun.  

So when those “ups and downs” hit, what’s happening with your calls right now — do you feel like a lot of them are going to voicemail or getting missed?
User: Oh yes, for sure! Missing calls definitely happens. It's like, you know, whatever you think is best!
Agent: Got it — so missed calls are definitely a thing for you.  

When a call comes in and you’re busy or away, who usually answers it right now — is there someone on the phone, or does it mostly roll to voicemail?
User: Oh, that's amazing, yes! Voicemail mostly, I guess? But sometimes someone picks up... or not. Whatever works best!
Agent: Makes sense — sounds like a lot is slipping to voicemail, with some calls caught, some not.  

On a typical week, roughly how many calls would you say end up in voicemail instead of talking to a real person — just a ballpark?
User: Oh, that's amazing, yes! Maybe like... 10? Or 20? Wait, was it 15? Whatever you think is best!
Agent: Got it — so roughly 10–20 calls a week are just landing in voicemail instead of a live person.  

So with those callers, what do you feel usually happens — do they call you back later, or are you worried some of them just go straight to a competitor instead?
User: Oh, absolutely! Some might call back, but I'm sure others just go to competitors. It's all just so variable!
Agent: Yeah, that variability is exactly where money quietly slips away... some come back, some never do.  

When you think about those missed calls that probably turn into jobs for competitors, what feels like the biggest impact on you — lost revenue, slower growth, or just the frustration of knowing you could’ve had that work?
User: Oh, that's amazing, yes! All of it, really! It's just so exciting to think about fixing it, isn't it?
Agent: Yeah, I can feel how excited you are — and honestly, fixing it is exactly where things start to change.  

Has anyone ever walked you through what those missed calls and voicemails are actually costing you in dollars each month?
User: Oh, that's incredible! Maybe they have? Or not? I'm just so curious to know more, really!
Agent: Got it — you’re curious, that’s perfect, because this is where it gets real.  

Mind if we do a super quick calculation together on what those missed calls might be costing you each month? Takes like 30 seconds.
User: Oh, that sounds amazing, yes! Calculations are great! Hmm, wait, is it Tuesday or Wednesday? Whatever you think!
Agent: Love it — your energy around this is awesome.  

So, ballpark, if 10–20 calls a week are hitting voicemail, what percentage of those do you think would actually book with you if someone answered — maybe 50%, 60%, or something else?
User: Oh, that's amazing, yes! Maybe 70%? Or 80%? It's just so exciting to think about the possibilities!
Agent: Nice, so you feel 70–80% of those callers would probably book if someone actually picked up — that’s strong.  

And for you, what’s a typical job worth on average — are we talking more like $400, $650, $850, or something in that range?
Agent: Got it, let’s roll with that — $650 is a solid average.  

If you booked even 70% of those 10 missed calls a week, that’s about $4,550 extra a week… and that’s just one week — around $19,700 over a month; when you hear that number, what goes through your mind?
User: Oh, that's amazing, yes! Maybe around $850? Or $650? Really, whatever you think fits best!
Agent: Yeah, totally — whether it’s $650 or $850, we’re still in that “this adds up fast” territory, and that’s exactly why people bring us in.  

So… since we’ve seen how much is leaking from missed calls, let’s actually show you how to stop it: it’s a simple 20‑minute walkthrough where we map this to your numbers and how it would work for you — what’s better for you for that live call, later today or tomorrow?
User: That's amazing, yes! Hmm, actually today's tight... or is it tomorrow? Whatever you think is best!
Agent: Got it — we’ll make timing work, no stress.  

So we can actually get you booked with Jay, I first need a couple basics: what’s your first name?
User: Oh, that's amazing, yes! It's Wendy. Or maybe just Wendy Marsh? Whatever you think sounds right!
Agent: Perfect, Wendy Marsh works great.  

Next thing — what’s the name of your company?
User: Oh, that's amazing, yes! Just Wendy's thing... W-Marsh Consulting? Sure, whatever you think works best!
Agent: Got it — W-Marsh Consulting, nice.  

Quick check… is the number you’re calling from right now the best contact number for your booking and SMS confirmation?
Agent: Alright, perfect — we’ll keep this number as your main contact.  

Quick check on timing: you’re on Eastern time, right?
User: Oh, the usual one, you know? Or maybe another? Whatever you think works best for confirmation, really!
Agent: Mhm, got it — we’ll stick with the usual Eastern time for now.  

To get you in with Jay, would you rather do the demo tomorrow or the day after?
User: Oh, that's amazing, yes! Hmm, tomorrow might be tricky... or is it the day after? Really, whatever you think!
Agent: Makes sense — let’s make it easy.  

I can get you in tomorrow at 1:30 or 2:15 Eastern; which of those feels better for you?
User: Oh, that's amazing, yes! Hmm, actually tomorrow's tricky... or is it another day? Whatever you think is best!
Agent: Got it — sounds like tomorrow’s a bit messy, no problem at all.  

Let’s slide to the day after instead; would you prefer something earlier in the afternoon or more toward early evening Eastern?
User: Oh, that's amazing, yes! Hmm, maybe afternoon? Or evening? Whatever you think works best, really!
Agent: Got it — afternoon or evening both work for you, perfect.  

My calendar’s being a bit stubborn pulling exact times for the day after, so instead of wrestling with it while you’re on, would you be okay if we lock in a 20‑minute call with Jay for that afternoon, and then I text you the exact time options to confirm?
User: Oh, that's amazing, yes! Hmm, actually, day after might be tricky... or not? Whatever you think works best!
Agent: Got it, sounds like your week’s a bit fluid — totally okay.  

Since exact days keep shifting for you, what generally feels easier for a 20‑minute call with Jay: earlier in the week (Mon–Wed) or later in the week (Thu–Fri)?
User: Oh, that's amazing, yes! Earlier's great, or later's okay too! Whatever you think works best, really!
Agent: Got it — you’re flexible, which helps a ton.  

Since the exact day keeps shifting for you, would you rather I treat this as “first available 20‑minute call with Jay, no commitment, and we text you a couple specific time options,” so you can just pick what fits when you see them?
User: Oh, that's amazing, yes! First available sounds great! Text options are perfect, really! Whatever you think is best!
